claims.text: Antidote for methemoglobin-forming agents (eg, some local anesthetics, nitrates, nitrites, sulfonamides)
claims.quote: Methemoglobin-forming agents (eg, aniline dyes, some local anesthetics, nitrates, nitrites, phenacetin, sulfonamides) | | Methylene blue

claims.text: MOA: reduced to leukomethylene blue (NADPH-dependent), which reduces methemoglobin back to hemoglobin
claims.quote: Methylene blue is reduced to leukomethylene blue by erythrocyte methemoglobin reductase in the presence of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH). Leukomethylene blue then reduces methemoglobin to oxyhemoglobin.

claims.text: Indication: MetHb >20–25%, or lower levels with symptoms
claims.quote: Methylene blue is indicated in patients with methemoglobin levels >20-25%, or who have lower levels but are symptomatic.

claims.text: Dose: 1–2 mg/kg IV over 5 min; may repeat in 1 h if cyanosis persists
claims.quote: Dosing: Adults and children: 1-2 mg/kg (0.1-0.2 ml/kg of 1% solution) intravenously infused over 5 minutes. Methylene blue has a rapid onset of action; maximal effects are normally seen within 30 minutes. The dose may be repeated in 1 hour if cyanosis persists.

claims.text: Caution: hemolysis (esp. G6PD deficiency, neonates); MAOI activity → serotonin syndrome with serotonergic drugs; CI severe renal impairment
claims.quote: Hemolysis can occur, especially in neonates. Patients with G6PD deficiency are more likely to develop hemolysis and methemoglobin production; therefore, judicious use is warranted. Extravasation results in local pain and tissue necrosis. Methylene blue has MAOI activity; therefore, concomitant use of methylene blue with serotonergic drugs (e.g. selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors, tricyclic antidepressants, norepinephrine-dopamine reuptake inhibitors, triptans, ergot alkaloids) may increase the risk of serotonin syndrome. Methylene blue is contraindicated in patients with severe renal impairment.
